items.name: Set rules AI follows every time
items.tagline: Custom instructions, preferences or a global CLAUDE.md.
items.cover_line: Tells the AI once how to work.
items.adds_over_previous: User-written instructions stored at account or user level are applied automatically to every new conversation without being retyped.
variants: ChatGPT custom instructions / personalization fields
claude.ai profile preferences
user-level instruction file a coding agent loads in every project (user CLAUDE.md, global AGENTS.md, Cursor user rules)

detect.present_if: An account-level or user-level instruction set exists with at least 1 rule written by the person or generated at their request (blocks that an installer or plugin added, such as a tool's list of commands, do not count), it applies to all conversations or all projects (not one), AND in the window it was active in at least 1 session (an 'instructions active' marker, the file shown as loaded, or the assistant visibly applying one of the person's rules) or the person created or edited it in the window.

claude-code: user-level CLAUDE.md shown as loaded at session start
reply visibly applies one of its specific rules
codex: global AGENTS.md or instructions in ~/.codex loaded
cursor: User Rules in settings applied in agent sessions
claude-ai: 'profile preferences active' marker
assistant applies a specific preference unprompted
chatgpt: 'custom instructions active' marker
assistant applies a specific instruction unprompted
config: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, Cursor user rules with user-written text and mtime in window

absent_if: The user only discusses, plans or asks about it.
It appears only in pasted third-party text or in the assistant's explanation/offer that the user did not take up.
The assistant or tool did it on its own default, without the user's request, config or script causing it.
Configured but neither fired nor used in the window.
Instructions scoped to one project, repository or workspace only (that is per-project-instructions).
The user pastes the same preamble at the start of chats instead of storing it (that is reusable-prompt-templates).
Only built-in memory entries exist, with no user-written instruction text (that is ask-to-remember).
Instruction text was drafted in a chat but there is no sign it was saved into settings or a user-level file.
probes: Does an account-level or user-level instruction set with user-caused content exist?
Does it apply to all conversations or projects rather than to a single project?
In the window, was it loaded or active in at least 1 session, or created or edited by the user?

teach.why: Every chat starts already knowing who you are and how you like answers.

items.name: Keep a rulebook citing past mistakes
items.tagline: 10+ rules for agents, 3+ naming what went wrong; revised.
items.cover_line: Keeps a rulebook for every agent.
items.adds_over_previous: The standing instructions become a maintained manual of rules, each tied to a concrete precedent or reason, that the user revises repeatedly as new failure cases arise.
variants: user-level instruction file organised as rules with precedents or examples
personal skill describing how to work with the user, loaded in every session
account-level instructions kept as numbered rules with dated revisions

detect.present_if: A user-level instruction file, personal skill, or account instruction set about how agents must work with this user exists that contains at least 10 distinct behavioural rules, ties at least 3 of them to a concrete past incident or worked example (a generic 'because' does not count; this rule-plus-precedent structure is what separates it from personal-instructions), and has been revised at least once after it was first written; it was loaded or revised in the window.

claude-code: personal skill or user CLAUDE.md loaded or injected at session start
session in which the user or agent edits it
codex: global AGENTS.md or personal skill loaded in codex sessions
claude-ai: profile preferences written as numbered rules with reasons
chatgpt: custom instructions written as numbered rules with reasons
config: rules file with 'why' or 'precedent' lines
git history or dated 'revised' entries showing more than one version

absent_if: The user only discusses, plans or asks about it.
It appears only in pasted third-party text or in the assistant's explanation/offer that the user did not take up.
The assistant or tool did it on its own default, without the user's request, config or script causing it.
Configured but neither fired nor used in the window.
A short preferences blurb (role, tone, length) without the rule-plus-precedent structure (that is personal-instructions).
The file describes a codebase's conventions for one project rather than how agents must work with the user (that is per-project-instructions).
The file was written in one go and has no later revision.
probes: Is there a user-level file, personal skill or account instruction set about how agents must work with this user?
Does it contain at least 10 behavioural rules, at least 3 tied to a concrete past incident or worked example?
Has it been revised at least once after creation (history, dated entries, timestamps or an edit session)?
Was it loaded or revised in the window?

teach.why: Every mistake an agent made with you becomes a rule no future agent repeats.

items.name: Turn your past chats into rules
items.tagline: Have AI read 10+ of your old sessions and write your rules.
items.cover_line: Turns past frustrations into rules.
items.adds_over_previous: The instructions are derived by having an AI analyse the user's own past sessions (corrections, frustrations, measured statistics) instead of being written from the user's memory.
variants: frustration and correction mining across local agent logs or chat exports
per-model failure priors derived from where each model went wrong for the user
thresholds set from measured statistics of the user's sessions
glossary of the user's recurring phrases and what they mean

detect.present_if: At the person's request, an agent reads or analyses at least 10 of the person's own past sessions, transcripts or logs, and the findings are written into, or used to edit, the person's standing instructions, operating manual, or a skill that loads by default. A tool reading sessions for its own report, UserRank's scan included, is not this analysis. Present if that analysis happened in the window, or if the resulting instruction file (recognisable by rules citing counts, frequencies or incidents produced by the analysis) was loaded in at least 1 session in the window.

claude-code: session where the agent reads many local session logs and writes rules from them
codex: codex session reading ~/.codex/sessions or other agents' logs to derive rules
cursor: agent reading exported chats to derive rules
claude-ai: past-chat search used to derive standing preferences
chatgpt: chat-history reference used, on request, to write custom instructions
config: instruction file whose rules cite counts, frequencies or incidents from the user's own sessions

absent_if: The user only discusses, plans or asks about it.
It appears only in pasted third-party text or in the assistant's explanation/offer that the user did not take up.
The assistant or tool did it on its own default, without the user's request, config or script causing it.
Configured but neither fired nor used in the window.
The user writes rules from memory or dictates them to the AI (that is self-authored-operating-manual).
Past sessions are analysed only for a report or summary, and nothing is written into standing instructions.
The analysed sessions belong to someone else or are synthetic.
Built-in memory learned preferences from chats automatically, without the user asking for an analysis.
A single correction in the current session is turned into a rule (that is correction-to-rule).
probes: Did the user ask an agent to analyse at least 10 of their own past sessions or logs?
Were the findings written into standing instructions, an operating manual, or a default-loaded skill?
Did the analysis happen in the window, or were the resulting instructions loaded in a session in the window?

teach.why: Your history remembers frustrations you forgot; rules built from it fix them.

items.name: Auto-reload your rules after compaction
items.tagline: A hook prints your rules at start, resume and compaction.
items.cover_line: Makes sure agents never lose the rules.
items.adds_over_previous: A lifecycle hook programmatically injects the instructions at session start, resume or context compaction, instead of relying on the host's normal instruction loading.
variants: session-start hook that prints the manual into context
hook on resume or compaction that re-injects the instructions
wrapper script that prepends the instructions to every agent run

detect.present_if: A hook (or wrapper script) that the person configured themselves, in user or project agent settings, runs on session start, resume or compaction and outputs instruction text the person wrote (or the contents of their own instruction file) into the agent's context, AND it fired in at least 1 session in the window (its injected output visible in the session or logs). A plugin's start hook that injects the plugin's own text does not count.

claude-code: SessionStart / compaction hook output containing the instructions at the top of sessions
codex: wrapper or hook that prepends the instruction file to each run
config: hooks in settings.json on SessionStart/PreCompact that cat an instruction file
hook log lines in window

absent_if: The user only discusses, plans or asks about it.
It appears only in pasted third-party text or in the assistant's explanation/offer that the user did not take up.
The assistant or tool did it on its own default, without the user's request, config or script causing it.
Configured but neither fired nor used in the window.
Instructions are loaded only by the host's native instruction-file loading, with no user-configured hook (that is personal-instructions or per-project-instructions).
Hooks exist but do something else (formatting, linting, notifications, checking replies).
A hook retrieves knowledge matches for each prompt rather than injecting the instructions (that is prompt-time-retrieval-hook).
probes: Is there a user-configured hook or wrapper on start, resume or compaction?
Does it inject instruction text into the agent's context?
Did it fire in at least 1 session in the window?

teach.why: Long sessions forget their rules when compacted; a hook puts them back.

items.name: Set rules AI follows per project
items.tagline: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or a Project's instructions.
items.cover_line: Briefs every project's agents up front.
items.adds_over_previous: Instructions scoped to one project, repository or workspace are stored where every session in that scope loads them automatically.
variants: repository instruction file (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .cursor/rules)
local, untracked instruction file propagated to each workspace
workspace prelude prepended to every agent session
ChatGPT Project or claude.ai Project instructions

detect.present_if: A project-, repository- or workspace-scoped instruction set exists that the user created or edited at least once (themselves or by asking an agent), AND in the window it was loaded in at least 1 session in that scope and was created or edited in the window, or it was loaded in at least 2 sessions in the window.

claude-code: project CLAUDE.md shown as loaded
edits to it in a session
codex: AGENTS.md loaded in codex sessions
cursor: .cursor/rules files applied, cited by the agent
claude-ai: Project with instruction text; sessions run inside it
chatgpt: Project with instructions; sessions run inside it
config: CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / .cursor/rules created or edited by the user (git author or edit session)

absent_if: The user only discusses, plans or asks about it.
It appears only in pasted third-party text or in the assistant's explanation/offer that the user did not take up.
The assistant or tool did it on its own default, without the user's request, config or script causing it.
Configured but neither fired nor used in the window.
Account-wide instructions that apply to all chats (that is personal-instructions).
A project that holds only uploaded files, with no instruction text (that is project-knowledge-files).
A README or docs file that agents are not configured to load automatically.
An instruction file in a repository that the user never created or edited (someone else's default).
probes: Is there a project- or workspace-scoped instruction set that the user created or edited?
Is it loaded automatically by sessions in that scope?
In the window, was it loaded and edited, or loaded in at least 2 sessions?

teach.why: Each project's rules are written once; every agent there starts informed.

items.name: Ask the AI to remember
items.tagline: Say 'remember that I...'; it shows 'memory updated'.
items.cover_line: Teaches the AI facts that stick.
items.adds_over_previous: The user explicitly writes a fact or preference into the assistant's persistent memory so later sessions can use it.
variants: 'remember that...' with ChatGPT or claude.ai memory
memory command or tool in a coding agent that writes to its user-level memory store

detect.present_if: In at least 2 sessions in the window, either (a) the user explicitly asks the assistant to remember or save a fact or preference for future chats and a memory write is confirmed (a 'memory updated' marker or a memory tool call), or (b) the assistant uses a memory the user wrote in that way; at least 1 of these sessions is of type (a).

claude-code: user says 'remember ...' and a memory file or memory entry is written
codex: user asks to remember and a memory note is written
cursor: user asks to remember and a Cursor memory is saved
claude-ai: 'remember this' plus memory update confirmation
later recall of that memory
chatgpt: 'Memory updated' marker after a user request
later recall of that memory
config: memory files whose entries match an explicit user request

absent_if: The user only discusses, plans or asks about it.
It appears only in pasted third-party text or in the assistant's explanation/offer that the user did not take up.
The assistant or tool did it on its own default, without the user's request, config or script causing it.
Configured but neither fired nor used in the window.
Memory was written or chat history referenced automatically by the assistant without the user asking.
The user asks whether memory exists or how it works, without writing to it.
The user asks the agent to study material and save its own synthesis (that is understand-and-memorize-on-demand).
The fact is added to a project instruction file (that is per-project-instructions).
probes: Did the user explicitly ask the assistant to remember something for future chats, with the write confirmed?
Counting those sessions and sessions where such a memory was used, are there at least 2 in the window?

teach.why: Facts you state once stop needing to be restated in every chat.

items.name: Have AI save its findings for later
items.tagline: Say 'read this code, then save what you learned to memory'.
items.cover_line: Has agents study, then remember.
items.adds_over_previous: The user asks the agent to study a body of material and persist its own synthesis into a memory or skill file it will reload, rather than storing a single fact the user stated.
variants: agent keeps typed memory files (about the user, the project, feedback, references)
dated lessons file written after a failure
'understand how X works and save it as a skill'

detect.present_if: The user asks the agent to investigate or read something (code, documents, a system, a past failure, a research topic) AND to keep what it learned for later, and the agent writes its own synthesis (not text the user dictated) into a memory file, memory store, knowledge store or skill, in at least 1 session in the window.

claude-code: user asks 'understand X and memorize it / save it for later'
Write to a memory or knowledge file or new SKILL.md with the agent's synthesis
codex: same request with the synthesis written to a memory or notes file
cursor: same request with a Cursor memory or notes file written
claude-ai: user asks to study a document and save a synthesis to memory
chatgpt: user asks to study material and save a synthesis; 'Memory updated'
config: memory or knowledge entries whose content is a synthesis of sources, created on a dated request

absent_if: The user only discusses, plans or asks about it.
It appears only in pasted third-party text or in the assistant's explanation/offer that the user did not take up.
The assistant or tool did it on its own default, without the user's request, config or script causing it.
Configured but neither fired nor used in the window.
The user dictates the fact to be stored (that is ask-to-remember).
The agent's automatic memory saved notes without the user asking.
What is saved is the status of the current task for the next session (that is agent-written-handoff).
What is saved is a rule derived from a user correction (that is correction-to-rule).
The synthesis is written only into a project instruction file as project rules or conventions (that is per-project-instructions).
probes: Did the user ask the agent both to learn or study something and to persist it for later?
Did the agent write its own synthesis into a memory, knowledge store or skill?
Did this happen in at least 1 session in the window?

teach.why: Its understanding outlives the session, so you never pay twice for the same digging.

items.name: Save corrections as lasting rules
items.tagline: After you correct it, add the fix to its instructions.
items.cover_line: Never corrects the same mistake twice.
items.adds_over_previous: Each correction is written, in the same session, as a durable rule that keeps the user's words and the precedent that triggered it.
variants: user edits the instruction file right after correcting the agent
standing instruction obliging the agent to propose and save a rule after each correction
correction saved to memory as a rule with the incident attached

detect.present_if: In at least 2 sessions in the window, after the person corrects the agent's behaviour, a rule capturing that specific correction is added to standing instructions, an operating manual, a skill or memory (in the same or the next session), by the person, by the agent at the person's request, or by the agent under a standing instruction the person wrote requiring it (a memory product or plugin that saves corrections on its own credits that tool).

claude-code: correction message followed by an Edit to CLAUDE.md, a skill or a memory file
codex: correction followed by an AGENTS.md or skill edit
cursor: correction followed by a rules-file edit
claude-ai: correction followed by a memory or preference update the user asked for
chatgpt: correction followed by 'Memory updated' at the user's request
config: rule entries whose wording matches a correction, with date or incident

absent_if: The user only discusses, plans or asks about it.
It appears only in pasted third-party text or in the assistant's explanation/offer that the user did not take up.
The assistant or tool did it on its own default, without the user's request, config or script causing it.
Configured but neither fired nor used in the window.
The user corrects the agent but nothing is persisted.
A preference stated proactively, not after a correction (that is ask-to-remember or personal-instructions).
Rules mined in bulk from many past sessions (that is instructions-mined-from-own-history).
The correction was saved by the agent's automatic memory without the user's request or standing instruction.
Edits to a scheduled task's prompt or to a one-off prompt (not standing instructions, a skill or memory).
probes: Did the user correct the agent's behaviour?
Was a rule capturing that correction then persisted, caused by the user or by their standing instruction?
Did this happen in at least 2 sessions in the window?

teach.why: A correction you make once is never needed again.

items.name: Test rule changes by replaying past prompts
items.tagline: Rerun 3+ past prompts with old and new rules; compare.
items.cover_line: Tests rule changes on real sessions.
items.adds_over_previous: A proposed change to standing instructions is validated by re-running real past sessions under the old and the new instructions and comparing the outcomes.
variants: headless re-runs of past prompts with and without the new rule
replaying full past sessions turn by turn under both instruction versions

detect.present_if: In the window, at the user's request, an agent re-runs at least 3 real prompts or sessions taken from the user's own history twice each, once with the old instructions and once with the changed instructions, produces a comparison of outcomes, and the change is then kept or reverted with reference to that comparison.

claude-code: claude -p runs or forked sessions comparing old and new instruction versions on past prompts
codex: codex exec runs comparing instruction versions
config: replay folder or report with old vs new results on real past sessions

absent_if: The user only discusses, plans or asks about it.
It appears only in pasted third-party text or in the assistant's explanation/offer that the user did not take up.
The assistant or tool did it on its own default, without the user's request, config or script causing it.
Configured but neither fired nor used in the window.
A single ad-hoc retry of one prompt after editing instructions.
Replaying an end user's session to debug a product (that is replay-real-failure).
The instruction change is tested only on synthetic scenarios (that is persona-scenario-evals or ab-with-control).
probes: Was an instruction change tested by re-running at least 3 real past prompts or sessions of the user's?
Was each run under both old and new instructions, with a comparison produced?
Was the change kept or reverted with reference to the comparison, in the window?

teach.why: Rule changes that feel right can make things worse; replay shows which.

items.name: Train a skill on replays of your sessions
items.tagline: Hill climbing: mine frustrations, replay, judge, revise.
items.cover_line: Hill-climbs rules on replayed sessions.
items.adds_over_previous: The replay comparison becomes a loop: failure modes mined from the person's own past frustrations are the judge's criteria, and the instruction file is revised and replayed round after round until the scores stop improving.
variants: a skill about working with the person, scored on replays of their past sessions until a round gains nothing
frustrations mined into failure modes, then judged replay rounds of a standing instruction file with a stop rule

detect.present_if: In the window, at the person's request or under a skill or script they wrote: (1) an agent extracts the frustrations or corrections the person expressed across at least 10 of their own past sessions and groups them into named failure modes; (2) a skill or standing instruction file is written or revised from those failure modes; (3) at least 2 rounds follow in which prompts or sessions from the person's own history are replayed with the current version of that file, a judge (a model or a script) scores each replay against the failure modes, and the file is revised between rounds; the loop ends on a stated stop rule (no gain, a plateau, a target score) or when a round gains nothing. The per-round scores are visible in a log, table or report. Repeated judged rounds until no further gain are what separate it from replay-to-prove-instruction-change (one old-against-new comparison).

claude-code: session reading many local session logs and listing the person's frustrations grouped into failure modes
claude -p or forked replays of past prompts with the skill, scored by a judge, over several rounds
a per-round score table and edits to the skill between rounds
codex: codex exec replays of past prompts with the revised AGENTS.md or skill, scored per round
config: skill or instruction file whose history shows revisions tied to replay scores

absent_if: The user only discusses, plans or asks about it.
It appears only in pasted third-party text or in the assistant's explanation/offer that the user did not take up.
The assistant or tool did it on its own default, without the user's request, config or script causing it.
Configured but neither fired nor used in the window.
One old-against-new comparison of an instruction change (that is replay-to-prove-instruction-change).
Rules written from an analysis of past sessions with no replay (that is instructions-mined-from-own-history).
Rounds of improvement on a score that does not come from failure modes mined from the person's own sessions (that is measurable-stop-rule).
Replays of synthetic sessions or of other people's sessions.
probes: Did an agent, at the person's request, group frustrations from 10+ of their own past sessions into failure modes?
Was a skill or standing instruction file written or revised from those failure modes?
Were past prompts replayed with it and judged against the failure modes, with the file revised, for 2+ rounds until a stop rule or no gain?

teach.why: Your rules about working with you get better every round, measured on your own history.

claude-code: Skill tool calls
typed custom slash commands
plugin skills firing
codex: custom prompts or skills invoked
claude-ai: skill invocation in a chat
chatgpt: chat opened inside a custom GPT
config: installed skills, plugins or commands folders

It appears only in pasted third-party text or in the assistant's explanation/offer that the user did not take up.
The assistant or tool did it on its own default, without the user's request, config or script causing it.
Configured but neither fired nor used in the window.
Only host built-in system commands such as clear, compact, model, init or help.
Skill or command invocations visible only in pasted logs or screenshots from someone else.
A prompt kept in notes and pasted by hand (that is reusable-prompt-templates).

items.name: Save a good prompt and reuse it

claude-ai: same pasted template block, often with a version label
chatgpt: same pasted template block, often with a version label

The assistant or tool did it on its own default, without the user's request, config or script causing it.
Configured but neither fired nor used in the window.

items.name: Build your own skills or GPTs

items.name: Share your skills with your team
items.tagline: A skills repo or plugin marketplace teammates install from.
items.cover_line: Ships skills to the whole team.
items.adds_over_previous: The skills live in a shared, versioned repository with an install or update mechanism that puts them into teammates' agent setups, rather than only in the user's own setup.
variants: git repository plus install script that links skills into each agent folder

items.adds_over_previous: The user consistently sends different kinds of tasks to different assistants or models according to their strengths.
variants: chat assistant for questions, coding agent for code
one assistant for its connectors, another for its memory or analysis

detect.present_if: The user uses at least 2 different assistants or models in the window with a recurring routing pattern: either (a) in at least 2 sessions the user explicitly sends a kind of task to a named other assistant or model (for example 'have the other vendor's CLI review this'), or (b) one task type is sent only to assistant A in at least 2 sessions AND another task type is sent only to assistant B in at least 2 sessions (a two-way split).

aggregate.per_session_line: routing: <session id> | <assistant> | <kinds_of_work value> | <explicit target assistant or none>

metrics.assistants_used: Number of distinct assistants (surface, or a named model the user chose) that appear in routing lines for human sessions in the window.
metrics.explicit_route_sessions: Number of sessions whose routing line names an explicit target assistant different from the session's own.
metrics.two_way_split: 1 if there are kinds A and B (A different from B) and assistants X and Y (X different from Y) such that every routing line with kind A names X and there are at least 2 of them, and every routing line with kind B names Y and there are at least 2 of them; otherwise 0.

claude-code: user asks the agent to hand a task to another vendor's CLI
Claude Code used for a task type absent elsewhere
codex: codex sessions used for a recurring task type
cursor: cursor used for a recurring task type
claude-ai: claude.ai used for a recurring task type
chatgpt: ChatGPT used for a recurring task type

absent_if: The user only discusses, plans or asks about it.
It appears only in pasted third-party text or in the assistant's explanation/offer that the user did not take up.
The assistant or tool did it on its own default, without the user's request, config or script causing it.
Configured but neither fired nor used in the window.
Two assistants used for the same kinds of task with no pattern.
The host selects the model automatically.
probes: Does the user use at least 2 assistants or models in the window?
Does the user explicitly route a kind of task to a named assistant in at least 2 sessions, or is there a consistent split by task type?

teach.why: Each assistant does what it is best at.

items.name: Use a different model for each role
items.tagline: In a script or agent file: one model plans, another judges.
items.cover_line: Casts a model for each role.
items.adds_over_previous: Within one workflow, distinct roles (planner, builder, reviewer or judge, simulated user) are explicitly assigned to different models.
variants: subagent definitions with a model field per role
script that generates with one model and judges with another

detect.present_if: An agent definition, skill, script or prompt that the person created (or had created at their request), not one supplied by an installed plugin, names different models for at least 2 roles in the same workflow, AND those roles ran with those models in at least 1 session in the window.

claude-code: subagent definitions with model fields
scripts calling claude -p --model X and another model as judge
codex: codex exec -m used for one role inside a workflow
config: agent definitions or eval configs mapping roles to models

absent_if: The user only discusses, plans or asks about it.
It appears only in pasted third-party text or in the assistant's explanation/offer that the user did not take up.
The assistant or tool did it on its own default, without the user's request, config or script causing it.
Configured but neither fired nor used in the window.
Switching models between unrelated chats (that is multi-assistant-routing).
The host routes models automatically.
probes: Does a user-caused definition, script or prompt name different models for at least 2 roles in one workflow?
Did those roles run with those models in at least 1 session in the window?

teach.why: Cheap models do the bulk, strong ones judge, and costs drop without losing quality.

items.name: Tell the agent it is authorized
items.tagline: Type 'you may ... without asking; it's my own account'.
items.cover_line: Spells out what agents may do.
items.adds_over_previous: The prompt explicitly grants authority for named actions or a named scope, and states the legitimate context (ownership, permission), so the agent proceeds without hedging or asking at each step.
variants: 'you are authorized to ... without asking'
'this is my own system or account; you have my permission to ...'

detect.present_if: In at least 2 sessions in the window, before the agent performs an action, the user's prompt contains an explicit grant of authority for a named action or scope ('you are authorized to', 'you have my permission to', 'you may ... without asking') or states the user's ownership or permission for the target system.

claude-code: 'you are authorized to', 'you have my permission', 'without asking' in user prompts
codex: same phrasing in codex prompts
claude-ai: same phrasing in chats
chatgpt: same phrasing in chats

absent_if: The user only discusses, plans or asks about it.
It appears only in pasted third-party text or in the assistant's explanation/offer that the user did not take up.
The assistant or tool did it on its own default, without the user's request, config or script causing it.
Configured but neither fired nor used in the window.
Answering yes when the agent asks for permission for a single action.
Tool permissions configured in settings (that is pre-approved-permissions).
A full written contract with forbidden actions and escalation and stop conditions (that is rules-of-engagement).
False or role-play framing used to get around a refusal.
probes: Did the user's prompt grant authority for a named action or scope, or state ownership or permission, before the action?
Did this happen in at least 2 sessions in the window?

teach.why: Clear authority up front stops the agent stalling on every step.

items.name: Write rules before agents run alone
items.tagline: Write what's forbidden, when to ask, when to stop.
items.cover_line: Writes the rules before letting go.
items.adds_over_previous: Before an autonomous run, the user gives a written contract covering allowed actions, forbidden actions, when to escalate and when to stop.
variants: rules typed into the brief
rules-of-engagement file or skill loaded for autonomous runs

detect.present_if: In at least 2 sessions in the window, before an agent works multi-step without per-step approval, the person provides rules (typed, or as a file or skill the person wrote that the session loads; rules in an installed plugin's skill, a harness prompt or a file someone else wrote do not count) that, beyond granting permission, cover at least 2 of: forbidden actions, conditions to escalate or ask, conditions to stop.

claude-code: brief or loaded skill with ALLOWED / FORBIDDEN / ESCALATE / STOP style rules before a long run
codex: same in codex briefs
claude-ai: same in chat briefs
chatgpt: same in agent-mode briefs
config: rules-of-engagement file or skill

absent_if: The user only discusses, plans or asks about it.
It appears only in pasted third-party text or in the assistant's explanation/offer that the user did not take up.
The assistant or tool did it on its own default, without the user's request, config or script causing it.
Configured but neither fired nor used in the window.
A single grant of permission (that is authorization-framing).
General standing preferences not tied to an autonomous run (that is personal-instructions).
Tool allow or deny lists enforced in configuration (that is least-privilege-delegation).
probes: Before a multi-step autonomous run, did the user or their file or skill provide rules?
Do they cover at least 2 of forbidden actions, escalation conditions, stop conditions?
Did this happen in at least 2 sessions in the window?

teach.why: You can leave an agent alone because you decided in advance what it must never do.

items.name: Limit a subagent's tools and keys
items.tagline: Its config allows only the tools, folders or keys it needs.
items.cover_line: Gives each agent only what it needs.
items.adds_over_previous: Each delegated agent's scope is enforced in configuration (tool allow or deny lists, read-only credentials, directory limits) narrower than the parent's, rather than only stated in prose.
variants: subagent definition with a restricted tool list
read-only database role or token for a delegated agent
headless invocation with allowed-tools or sandbox flags

detect.present_if: A delegated-agent definition, subagent configuration, headless invocation or credential set that the person created (or had an agent create at their request), not a built-in or plugin-supplied agent, restricts that agent's tools, paths or credentials to a subset of the parent's, AND that restricted agent ran in at least 1 session in the window.

claude-code: claude -p with --allowedTools / --disallowedTools
subagent definitions with restricted tools
codex: codex exec -s read-only or restricted sandbox
config: agent definitions with tool lists
read-only roles or tokens for delegated agents

absent_if: The user only discusses, plans or asks about it.
It appears only in pasted third-party text or in the assistant's explanation/offer that the user did not take up.
The assistant or tool did it on its own default, without the user's request, config or script causing it.
Configured but neither fired nor used in the window.
Restrictions stated only in prose in the prompt (that is rules-of-engagement).
Global allow lists that widen what the agent can do (that is pre-approved-permissions).
Host-provided read-only subagent types used without any user configuration.
probes: Is there a user-caused configuration restricting a delegated agent's tools, paths or credentials?
Did that restricted agent run in at least 1 session in the window?

teach.why: A helper agent cannot do damage it was never given the tools for.

items.name: Have agents monitor long background jobs
items.tagline: Start tests in the background with a monitor; keep working.
items.cover_line: Keeps long jobs watched, not waited on.
items.adds_over_previous: Long-running jobs are started in the background with a monitor that reports progress or failure, so the agent continues other work instead of blocking or polling by hand.
variants: background process plus a monitor tool that wakes the agent
log tail with an alert condition

detect.present_if: In at least 2 sessions in the window, at the person's request or under an instruction the person wrote (the harness backgrounding a command on its own, or a system reminder suggesting a watcher, does not count), the agent starts a long-running process in the background (build, test suite, eval, deploy, crawl) together with a watcher (monitor tool, log tail with alert condition, timed check), does other work before the job finishes, and then acts on the watcher's report.

claude-code: Bash run_in_background plus a Monitor or watch step, agent continues and later reacts
codex: background process with a watcher

absent_if: The user only discusses, plans or asks about it.
It appears only in pasted third-party text or in the assistant's explanation/offer that the user did not take up.
The assistant or tool did it on its own default, without the user's request, config or script causing it.
Configured but neither fired nor used in the window.
The agent waits or blocks on the job.
A task scheduled to run later (that is scheduled-tasks).
A background job started without any watcher.
probes: Did the agent, at the user's request or instruction, start a background job with a watcher?
Did it do other work before the job finished and then act on the watcher's report?
Did this happen in at least 2 sessions in the window?

teach.why: Slow jobs stop eating the agent's time and yours.

items.name: Start a new chat from old output
items.tagline: Paste the old chat's plan or output into a fresh one.
items.cover_line: Carries context into fresh sessions.
items.adds_over_previous: The user moves context from an earlier AI session into a new one by pasting or attaching its transcript or outputs.
variants: pasting an earlier transcript excerpt
attaching an earlier output or plan file

detect.present_if: In at least 2 sessions in the window, the person's opening or early message pastes or attaches material produced in an earlier AI session (transcript excerpt, earlier output, earlier plan) in order to continue that work; a harness's automatic summary of a compacted or resumed session does not count.

claude-code: first user message pastes an earlier transcript, plan or output
@file of an earlier session's output
codex: same in codex sessions
claude-ai: opening message pastes or attaches an earlier chat's output
chatgpt: opening message pastes or attaches an earlier chat's output

absent_if: The user only discusses, plans or asks about it.
It appears only in pasted third-party text or in the assistant's explanation/offer that the user did not take up.
The assistant or tool did it on its own default, without the user's request, config or script causing it.
Configured but neither fired nor used in the window.
The assistant's memory or chat-history feature recalled the context automatically.
The pasted material is the user's own document, not produced in an AI session.
probes: Did the user paste or attach material produced in an earlier AI session?
Was it done to continue that work in a new session?
Did this happen in at least 2 sessions in the window?

teach.why: A fresh session with the right material beats a long, confused one.

items.name: Have AI write handovers between sessions
items.tagline: It writes a prompt or file a fresh session can run alone.
items.cover_line: Has each agent brief the next one.
items.adds_over_previous: The agent, not the user, writes a self-contained brief that a fresh agent can execute without the original conversation.
variants: brief saved to a file and the next agent told to read it
prompt written for the user to paste into a new session
lessons-learned document written to seed a clean rebuild
subagents return their results in files

detect.present_if: In at least 2 sessions in the window, the person asks the agent (or a skill the person wrote instructs it, or the person types a handoff command by name) to produce a brief, prompt or lessons document intended for another agent or a later session, and the agent produces it as a standalone text or file. A handoff a plugin writes on its own does not count.

claude-code: user asks for a handoff/brief/prompt for another agent; agent writes it to a file or block
codex: same in codex sessions
claude-ai: user asks for a prompt to paste into a new chat
chatgpt: user asks for a prompt to paste into a new chat
config: handoff or brief files written by agents

absent_if: The user only discusses, plans or asks about it.

The assistant or tool did it on its own default, without the user's request, config or script causing it.
Configured but neither fired nor used in the window.
The user writes the brief themselves or pastes old material (that is carry-context-forward).
An ordinary end-of-task summary not meant for another agent.
probes: Did the user or their skill ask for a brief or prompt intended for another agent or session?
Did the agent produce it as a standalone text or file?
Did this happen in at least 2 sessions in the window?

teach.why: The agent knows what it did; its handover lets the next session start informed.

items.name: Let an agent launch separate agent sessions
items.tagline: Not a subagent: a new terminal or cloud task with a prompt.
items.cover_line: Lets one agent launch the next.
items.adds_over_previous: The agent itself opens the next top-level session and hands it the brief, without the user copying or starting anything.
variants: agent starts a headless or terminal session with the brief as its prompt
agent creates a new workspace or cloud task through an orchestration tool

detect.present_if: An agent of the person's (at their request or under a skill or script the person wrote; an orchestration app or plugin that opens sessions by its own design does not count) starts a new top-level agent session (new terminal, workspace or cloud task, through a CLI, API or orchestration tool) with a written brief as its initial prompt, and that new session runs, on at least 1 occasion in the window.

claude-code: Bash call running claude -p or codex exec with a brief file
workspace or cloud-task creation tool calls with a prompt
codex: codex session launching another agent CLI with a brief
cursor: agent launching a background agent with a brief

absent_if: The user only discusses, plans or asks about it.

items.cover_line: Pre-clears the routine steps.
items.adds_over_previous: The user configures standing permissions so the agent performs listed actions without asking each time.

deploy token in the agent's environment
infrastructure MCP server with write access

infrastructure MCP write calls
codex: same in codex sessions
